query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a titanium dioxide (TiO2) coating via sol-gel deposition on stainless steel (SS) can enhance its corrosion resistance in extreme environments.
generation.material_initial_state: AISI 304 stainless steel in its annealed state
generation.intervention: Sol-gel deposition of titanium dioxide (TiO2) coating
generation.conditions: Coating thickness of 500 nm, heat treatment at 500°C for 1 hour
generation.mechanism: The TiO2 coating acts as a barrier, preventing the penetration of corrosive species to the stainless steel substrate, thereby reducing the corrosion rate
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in corrosion rate of at least 70% compared to uncoated stainless steel, measured in mm/year
generation.uncertainty: The actual corrosion resistance may vary depending on the specific deposition conditions, coating thickness, and heat treatment parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion corrosion test in 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the TiO2-coated stainless steel is not at least 50% lower than that of the uncoated stainless steel after 30 days of immersion, the hypothesis is falsified
